A high pitch droning heralds death for many mega-fauna that roam the Farplains, stampeding in terror from a tyrandroth on the 
hunt. Th e large dragonfly, a fortunately rare sight, as the predatory insects compete viciously with themselves for territory or mating 
couplings that end with the male being eviscerated by the larger females. Th is fi erce aerial hunter will often run down herds, singling 
out stragglers with its exothermic caustic chemical spray to blind and cripple them before descending and ripping apart flesh to feast. 
While this insect cannot hope to fly and survive when the murmurations of the maedrynn are at their height of savagery, the tyrandroth 
absolutely dominates the Farplains as a reigning apex predator for most of the year, only fearing another of its lethal kind.

Compound Vision Th e tyrandroth is capable of seeing in nearly 360 
degrees around itself and has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) 
checks that rely on sight.
Agile Flier When the tyrandroth makes a melee attack, it can 
immediately use its remaining movement speed to fly away. Th is 
doesn’t provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an 
enemy’s reach. 
Single Minded Th e tyrandroth has Advantage on Saving Th rows 
against the Charmed or Frightened Conditions.
Droning Flight When flying, the tyrandroth’s wings emit a loud 
droning sound that can be heard to a range of 200 ft., and while 
flying the tyrandroth has Disadvantage on Stealth checks.

Multiattack Th e tyrandroth makes two attacks with its Tetrad

Tetrad Mandibles Melee Attack Roll: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one

Hooked Tarsus Melee Attack Roll: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. 
Hit: 14 (2d10 + 5) Slashing damage. If the target is Medium or 
smaller, and the tyrandroth moved +30ft. toward it immediately 
before the hit, the target has the Grappled and Restrained 
condition (Escape DC 16). Th e tyrnadroth can move while 
grappling a creature but cannot use its Hooked Tarsus attack 
again until it releases the grappled creature.

Encountering Under the open sky of the Farplains, the loud 
resonating drone of a tyrandroth on the hunt can be heard far 
and wide. At the height of noon is when this gigantic insect is 
at its most dangerous, using the blinding sun to obscure its 
incoming attack. In the cool of night it settles into the boughs 
of the Wealdwoods and while high off the ground, it is much 
more vulnerable and can be caught unawares.
